result.text: Title: Blizzard Online Character Generator Blizzard creates a cool online tool for creating characters for their new WoW expansion.
When creating a World of Warcraft character, you can start doing two things: While you are setting up your account, you can already come up with good character names.
The setup of your account starts with checking whether you have a battle.net account.
If you do not have one yet, you enter the account information and click the link you receive in the confirmation mail.
As soon as you have a battle.net account, you can check if you have an active WoW subscription.
If not, you can select the payment method.
If you choose credit card, enter your credit card information.
If you choose your bank account, enter your IBAN and BIC numbers.
After that you can log into the game and select realm, race and class of your character.
Until now, you should have come up with some good names.
You enter them one by one until a name is still available.
You get a confirmation, and some selfies of your character, as soon as a expansion is released you get another message.

result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Use a parallel split when all outgoing branches start. Do not add decision conditions to parallel branches.
Use a parallel join when a shared continuation waits for all active parallel branches. Never use it to join mutually exclusive alternatives.
Use an inclusive split when one or more conditions can be true; use an inclusive join to synchronize only activated reachable branches.
Sequence flows may cross lanes in one process. Use message flows across participant pools, never between lanes.
An ordinary embedded subprocess participates in normal sequence flow and may contain its own starts, ends, activities, gateways and flows.

result.rule: When the description says that one activity can be carried out while another activity or sequence of activities is underway, and that both tracks must be complete before a later activity can proceed: Model the tracks as concurrent branches, using a parallel gateway to split them and a parallel gateway to synchronize them before the dependent activity.

When the description states that an activity is required while another activity may be performed only if a stated condition holds, and that the flow continues after the applicable work is complete: Model the activities as branches from an inclusive split, with the condition on the optional branch, and use an inclusive join to synchronize the branches that were activated before the dependent next step.

When the description states that an activity is followed by a decision, synchronization, or cycle-exit condition, or that concurrent work begins after a preceding activity: Connect the activity to the relevant gateway with a sequence flow; for concurrent work, route the preceding flow through a parallel gateway that starts the concurrent branches.

When the description identifies multiple required activities within a phase, requires all of them before that phase can end, and specifies no order among them: Model the activities as parallel branches synchronized by a parallel gateway.

result.rule: Use bpmn:callActivity only to invoke a separately defined reusable process or global task; make calledElement resolvable in the intended model context.
When the description does not justify a specialized construct, use the simplest compatible BPMN construct and do not guess missing semantics.
Use short, faithful labels in the input language. Prefer verb-object activity names and meaningful business triggers or outcomes for events.
Use bpmn:task for atomic work when the execution mode is unspecified. A task contains no internal flow.
Use bpmn:sendTask or bpmn:receiveTask when sending or waiting for a message is itself the modeled unit of work.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.

When the description states a specific activity, decision, or outcome: Label the corresponding BPMN element with wording that preserves the described action and its object or result; do not substitute a related but different action or outcome.

When the description states a core activity and separately describes a condition or later outcome that marks its completion: Label the BPMN activity with its core action and object; do not add the separately stated completion condition or later outcome to the activity label.
